input.prompt:
Explore this repository at /bench/repo to answer a specific question about third-party identity provider authentication (SSO / external identity providers / OAuth / OIDC / SAML).

I need to know:
1. Which package (directory/module) DEFINES the provider abstraction — i.e., the base interface/abstract class/type that identity providers implement (something like "IdentityProvider", "SSOProvider", "AuthProvider", etc.).
2. Which package ships a CONCRETE protocol implementation of that abstraction (e.g., an OIDC, SAML, LDAP, OAuth2 implementation package).

Please look at the top-level directory structure (packages/, apps/, libs/, etc.), package names, and grep for terms like "identity provider", "IdentityProvider", "SSOProvider", "OIDC", "OpenID", "SAML", "sso", "idp".

Report back:
- The exact package name/path that defines the abstraction (cite file paths).
- The exact package name/path of the concrete protocol implementation (cite file paths).
- Brief evidence (class/interface names, file contents) for each.

Be thorough — check naming conventions and multiple locations.

content.text:
I have all the evidence needed. This is the **memos** project (Go). Here are my findings.

## Summary

This repo (usememos/memos) implements third-party SSO through an `internal/idp` package that defines the shared abstraction, plus a nested `internal/idp/oauth2` subpackage that ships the one concrete protocol implementation (OAuth2). OAuth2 is currently the only wire protocol supported.

## 1. Package defining the provider abstraction

**Package path: `/bench/repo/internal/idp`** (Go import path `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp`)

- File `/bench/repo/internal/idp/idp.go` — this is the base package. It defines the shared, protocol-agnostic type that every concrete provider returns:
  ```go
  package idp

  type IdentityProviderUserInfo struct {
      Identifier  string
      DisplayName string
      Email       string
      AvatarURL   string
  }
  ```
  This is the abstraction contract in this codebase: the `idp` package owns the neutral `IdentityProviderUserInfo` type, and every protocol implementation lives under it and depends on it. Note the abstraction here is expressed as a shared return type + package boundary rather than a Go `interface`; there is no `interface`/abstract base declared. Concrete providers expose methods (`ExchangeToken`, `UserInfo`) that produce `idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo`.

The persisted/config-level provider model (type enum, config oneof) is generated separately under the proto/store layer, notably `/bench/repo/proto/gen/store/idp.pb.go`:
- `type IdentityProvider struct` (line 70)
- `type IdentityProvider_Type int32` with `IdentityProvider_OAUTH2 = 1` (lines 24–28) — the enum of supported provider types (OAUTH2 is the only real member besides UNSPECIFIED)
- `type IdentityProviderConfig struct` and `IdentityProviderConfig_Oauth2Config` (lines 154, 214)

## 2. Package shipping the concrete protocol implementation

**Package path: `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2`** (Go import path `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp/oauth2`)

- File `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go` — file-level doc comment: `// Package oauth2 implements the OAuth2 identity provider integration.`
  - `type IdentityProvider struct { config *storepb.OAuth2Config }` (line 20) — the concrete OAuth2 provider
  - `func NewIdentityProvider(config *storepb.OAuth2Config) (*IdentityProvider, error)` (line 27) — constructor
  - `func (p *IdentityProvider) ExchangeToken(ctx, redirectURL, code, codeVerifier string) (string, error)` (line 47) — OAuth2 code-for-token exchange, with PKCE support
  - `func (p *IdentityProvider) UserInfo(ctx, token string) (*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo, error)` (line 83) — calls the userinfo endpoint and maps claims into the base `idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo` type (confirming the dependency on the abstraction package)
- Test: `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2_test.go`

## Wiring evidence (how they connect)

- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go`
  - imports `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp/oauth2` (line 13)
  - `resolveSSOIdentity(...)` (line 104) instantiates the concrete provider: `oauth2.NewIdentityProvider(identityProvider.Config.GetOauth2Config())` (line 121)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service.go` calls `resolveSSOIdentity` during SSO sign-in (line 80)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/idp_service.go` is the CRUD gRPC service for identity providers; `convertIdentityProviderConfigToStore` branches on `v1pb.IdentityProvider_OAUTH2` (line 226), confirming OAuth2 is the only implemented type.

## Note on other protocols
Grepping for `OIDC`, `OpenID`, `SAML`, `LDAP` across the Go code returned no implementation packages — only OAuth2 exists. There is no `internal/idp/oidc`, `saml`, or `ldap` subpackage. So OAuth2 is the sole concrete protocol implementation.
